data.title: Sysco Declares Quarterly Dividend Payment
data.description:
HOUSTON, Nov. 13, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sysco Corporation today announced that the Board of Directors declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.55 per share, payable on January 29, 2027, to common stockholders of record at the close of business on January 8, 2027.

About Sysco

Sysco is the global leader in selling, marketing and distributing food and related products to customers who prepare meals away from home. This includes restaurants, healthcare and educational facilities, lodging establishments, entertainment venues, and more. Sysco operates 333 distribution centers, in 10 countries, with 75,000 colleagues serving approximately 670,000 customer locations. The company generated sales of more than $84 billion in fiscal year 2026 that ended June 27, 2026.

As the world’s largest food-away-from-home distributor, Sysco offers customized supply chain solutions, bespoke specialty product offerings, and culinary support to drive customers to innovate and optimize their operations. We act as a trusted business partner to our customers, helping them grow through our industry-leading portfolio that includes fresh produce, premium proteins, specialty products, sustainably focused items, equipment and supplies, and innovative culinary solutions.

For more information, visit www.sysco.com. For important news and key information for Sysco investors, visit the Investor Relations section of the company’s website at investors.sysco.com.

data.title: Nvidia results, Anthropic IPO pose tests for tumultuous AI trade
data.description:
Key points:
  • Nvidia results on Tuesday, following CEO's abrupt resignation
  • Anthropic shares expected to start trading on Thursday
  • Monthly retail sales, Fed minutes also due
  • Big week for retailer results: Walmart, Target, Home Depot

By Lewis Krauskopf

The AI trade that has fueled the rising stock market in recent years but has lately shown signs of vulnerability faces twin tests next week: the highly anticipated IPO of Anthropic and quarterly results from beleaguered semiconductor giant Nvidia.

Shares of Nvidia , whose chips have been at the center of the AI boom, tumbled this week after controversies emerged involving longtime CEO Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down on Thursday following revelations about two extramarital affairs, including one involving a suspected Chinese spy.

The issue left investors with major questions heading into Tuesday's high-stakes quarterly report.

Just two days later, trading in Claude chatbot creator Anthropic is expected to begin, setting up a real-time barometer for sentiment on the AI trade.

"The market has rose-colored glasses on almost all the risks," including inflation and the war in Iran, in addition to uncertainty over AI, said Sameer Samana, head of global equities and real assets at the Wells Fargo Investment Institute.

Disappointments next week, Samana said, "could finally kind of wake investors up from this ability to look at every glass as half full."

The AI trade wobbled in recent weeks following doubts over the sustainability of massive investment spending propelling the AI boom. Concerns flared after Democrats swept to victory in the midterm elections earlier this month over President Donald Trump's Republicans, a result that threatened more stringent regulations on the expansion of AI data centers.

Despite Nvidia's woes, many AI-linked stocks steadied in recent days, and the benchmark S&P 500 CBOE:SPX posted a weekly gain, after four straight weekly declines. The index was up 10.5% so far in 2026.

NVIDIA REPORTS UNDER NEW MANAGEMENT

Nvidia, which long reigned as the signature stock of the four-year-old US bull market, has seen its market capitalization drop from about $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion as of Friday, according to LSEG data.

Nvidia's still-significant market heft, combined with its position at the center of the AI ecosystem, means its results stand to ripple broadly. The extent to which Huang is tied to Nvidia's fortunes will be in the spotlight on Tuesday.

Pressure will be on interim CEO Colette Kress, previously Nvidia's chief financial officer, and the company to shore up investor confidence.

Analysts expect earnings growth of 90% on revenue of $109 billion in the company's fiscal third quarter, according to LSEG data.

Given the uncertainty swirling around Nvidia, "if they have less-than-stellar earnings, whatever penalty the market would apply is going to be leveraged down," said Alex Morris, CEO of F/m Investments.

ANTHROPIC SET TO DEBUT

Anthropic's initial public offering is set to value the company at up to $1.4 trillion, as the AI lab and some of its investors aim to raise up to $64.4 billion by selling 825 million shares.

Anthropic's Nasdaq listing comes on the heels of the high-profile June IPO for Elon Musk's SpaceX , which raised $75 billion at a nearly $1.75 trillion valuation.

SpaceX shares have had a bumpy few months. The stock last traded at about $139 compared with its IPO price of $135, after falling to about $105 in August.

"If you have Anthropic come out and then the IPO does poorly, I think that is probably another cautionary sign that investors are getting a little bit more stressed with the AI trade," said Patrick Ryan, chief investment strategist at Madison Investments.

CONSUMER IN FOCUS WITH RETAIL SALES, EARNINGS

The monthly US retail sales report on Tuesday stands out among the consequential economic data for markets next week. The report will give a view into the health of the US consumer as well as an indication of whether inflation is continuing to build and could lead to more aggressive rate hikes from the Federal Reserve.

Data this week showed consumer prices rose faster than expected in October, prompting markets to factor in more rate hikes in coming months. Minutes from the latest Fed meeting, to be released on Wednesday, also could shed light on the central bank's plans for further monetary tightening that could pressure equities.

A host of major retailers also report results next week, including Walmart , Target , Home Depot and Lowe's .

Investors are particularly eager for clues about whether consumer spending is holding up as Americans face higher gasoline prices stemming from the Middle East conflict and higher borrowing costs than earlier in the year.

"What I would want to see from consumer-oriented companies is ... have things taken another leg down given what is going on with energy prices remaining elevated and interest rates back at the highs," Samana said.

data.title: Nasdaq, S&P 500 Close In The Red But Dow Posts Modest Gain
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After recovering from an initial slump but still ending Thursday's session mostly lower, stocks showed a notable move back to the downside in early trading on Friday.

The Nasdaq and S&P 500 once again regained ground as the day progressed but closed in negative territory. The Nasdaq slid 229.82 points or 0.9 percent to 25,136.27 and the S&P 500 fell 30.73 points or 0.4 percent to 7,561.67.

The narrower Dow, on the other hand, spent much of the day lingering near the unchanged line before closing up 50.46 points or 0.1 percent to 52,347.55.

Despite closing lower for two straight days, the Nasdaq and the S&P 500 surged by 2.3 percent and 2.5 percent for the week, respectively. The Dow also shot up by 2.1 percent.

Weakness among technology stocks once again weighed on Wall Street, as reflected by the notable decline by the tech-heavy Nasdaq.

Shares of Nvidia (NVDA) showed another significant move to the downside, with the AI leader tumbling by 2 percent.

Shares of Nvidia recovered from an initial sell-off but still dove by more than 4 percent on Thursday following news CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO following the resignation of Jensen Huang.

Semiconductor stocks subsequently turned in some of the tech sector's worst performances, resulting in a 3.4 percent plunge by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index.

Computer hardware and networking stocks also saw considerable weakness, with the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index and the NYSE Arca Networking Index both tumbling by 2.6 percent.

Outside of the tech sector, airline stocks also saw some weakness, although energy stocks showed strong moves to the upside.

The weakness on Wall Street also came as treasury yields extended a recent surge following the release of the Labor Department's report on producer price inflation in the month of October.

While the report showed a slightly smaller-than-expected monthly increase in producer prices, the annual rate of producer price accelerated to 6.5 percent, the fastest pace of growth since November 2022.

'For equities, 6.5% producer inflation matters because companies can get squeezed from both sides,' said Chris Osmond, Chief Investment Officer for Fifth Third Wealth Advisors.

'Persistent input costs pressure margins, while higher bond yields raise the discount rate investors apply to those earnings,' he added. 'That combination puts a much higher hurdle on expensive stocks whose valuations depend on earnings far into the future.'

The report also indicated inflation is broadening beyond energy, as energy prices edged lower but food prices jumped and prices for services increased for a fifth consecutive month.

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved mostly lower on Friday. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index slumped by 1.6 percent and China's Shanghai Composite Index fell by 0.6 percent, although Japan's Nikkei 225 Index bucked the downtrend and rose by 0.5 percent.

Meanwhile, the major European markets turned in a mixed performance on the day. While the German DAX Index edged down by 0.1 percent, the French CAC 40 Index crept up by 0.1 percent and the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index climbed by 0.4 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries have extended the notable downward move seen over the two previous sessions. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, has jumped 5.3 basis points to 5.156 percent.

data.title: Empire Petroleum Files 8K - Entry Into Definitive Agreement >EP
data.description:
Empire Petroleum Corp. (EP) filed a Form 8K - Entry Into a Definitive Agreement - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on November 13, 2026.

On November 9, 2026, Empire Petroleum Corporation (the "Company") issued that certain Promissory Note in the aggregate principal amount of $6,750,000 (the "Note") to Energy Evolution Master Fund, Ltd., a Caymon Islands exempted company ("Energy Evolution"). As of November 9, 2026, Energy Evolution has advanced the Company $6,750,000 under the Note. The proceeds of the Note will be used by the Company for general working capital purposes.

The Note matures on May 9, 2028 (the "Maturity Date") and accrues interest at the rate of 6% per annum. After the Maturity Date, any principal balance of the Note remaining unpaid accrues interest at the rate of 9% per annum. All accrued but unpaid interest is payable in cash on the Maturity Date, except upon the occurrence of an Event of Default (as defined in the Note), in which case all accrued and unpaid interest shall immediately be due and payable.

All or any portion of the outstanding principal amount of the Note may be converted into shares of common stock of the Company at a conversion price of $2.16 per share (the "Conversion Price"), at the option of Energy Evolution, at any time and from time to time from the period beginning on January 9, 2027 and ending on the Maturity Date. If the full principal amount of the Note is converted into shares of common stock of the Company, 3,125,000 shares (the "Underlying Shares") would be issued. Accrued and unpaid interest on the principal amount converted is paid in cash on the date of conversion. The Conversion Price is subject to customary adjustments.

The Note may be prepaid at any time or from time to time without the consent of Energy Evolution and without penalty or premium, provided that the Company provides Energy Evolution with at least five business days prior written notice, each principal payment is made in cash and all accrued interest is paid in cash.

The Company will use commercially reasonable efforts to cause the NYSE American to approve a supplemental listing application related to the issuance of the Underlying Shares as soon as reasonably practicable.

For a description of any material relationship between the Company and Energy Evolution, see the Company's definitive proxy statement for its 2026 Annual Meeting of Stockholders filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the "SEC") on April 30, 2026 and the Company's Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 filed with the SEC on November 13, 2026.

The foregoing summary of the Note is qualified in its entirety by reference to the full terms and conditions of the Note, a copy of which is filed as Exhibit 10 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and is incorporated by reference into this Item 1.01.

The full text of this SEC filing can be retrieved at: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/887396/000107261326000891/emp_8k-19107.htm

Any exhibits and associated documents for this SEC filing can be retrieved at: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/887396/000107261326000891/0001072613-26-000891-index.htm

Public companies must file a Form 8-K, or current report, with the SEC generally within four days of any event that could materially affect a company's financial position or the value of its shares.
